# DRYDOCK P001: validation report (generated by drydock.py)

Every number here is computed from the CAD geometry by this run. Fit checks are boolean intersections of the real B-rep solids (volume of overlap in mm³). Force numbers are hand-calculation estimates, not test results. **Nothing here replaces a physical print-and-fit test.**

## Mechanics estimates (hand calculations, PETG E = 2000 MPa, μ = 0.25)

- Plug ring compliance (free thin ring, 3 point loads): 0.0203 mm/N. The real plug is fixed to the neck at one end, so it is stiffer than this: forces below are **lower bounds**.
- Detent: 0.25 mm radial flex, ramp 20°, ≥ 12 N per lug, twist torque ≥ 0.52 N·m to pass the bump The real torque is higher by an unknown factor (the plug is anchored to the neck); measure it on the fit gauge. Target: a deliberate wrist twist, comparable to opening a small jar.
- Pull-off with the cap locked: the plug would have to collapse 1.0 mm at every lug; lower bound ≈ 247 N (the cartridge weighs < 1 N).

## Capacity and airflow

- Internal cavity (both caps on, windows in): **72.5 mL**
- Usable fill (to the internal step below the top socket): **54.8 mL** ≈ 38–44 g of silica gel beads (bulk 0.70–0.80 g/mL)
- Water it can hold at equilibrium (Type A gel, ~10 % of its mass at 20 % RH, ~20 % at 40 % RH): ≈ 4.1 g at 20 % RH, ≈ 8.2 g at 40 % RH
- Open vent area: body 858 mm² (65 slots), cap faces 341 mm², total 1199 mm²
- Window viewing area: 308 mm² (two Ø14 windows)

## Bead containment (largest gap on every path out)

- Body vent slots: 1.2 mm wide · cap face slots: 1.2 mm
- Plug to socket: 0.2 mm radial · cap lift when locked: 0.2 mm
- Window to recess: 0.1 mm radial · body-to-body joint (coupler): ≤ 0.4 mm
- Smallest bead that cannot escape: about 1.5 mm (slot width plus print variation). Use 2–5 mm beads.
